home_meta_title: PadelIndex — Your level. Proven, not claimed.
home_meta_description: PadelIndex is the independent rating for amateur padel players. A Bayesian rating built for doubles, confirmed by your opponents, valid across every club. Try the match simulator to see how your rating moves.
home_og_description: A padel doubles rating from confirmed matches: opponent strength, score margin and confidence — not self-assessment.
home_hero_eyebrow: The rating for amateur padel players
home_hero_sub: PadelIndex measures how strong you really play — across club lines, from confirmed results, with a model built for doubles instead of chess.
home_problem_h2: Almost nobody really knows their level.
home_problem_p: Levels get guessed, ticked on a form, or handed out differently by every club. The moment you play somewhere else, the number means nothing. But the most common objection to a rating system checks out on paper — here it is.
home_gripe1_q: "I've clearly gotten better — the number just won't move."
home_gripe1_a: With PadelIndex your rating moves after every confirmed match, and you see exactly how much of that came from opponent strength, score margin, and your recent run.
home_gripe2_q: "That guy only plays in his own circle and suddenly he's at the top."
home_gripe2_a: Every result needs confirmation from the opposing team. Results without an opponent don't count — so made-up matches don't either.
home_gripe3_q: "Won 6:1, 6:2 and the rating didn't move at all. I don't get it."
home_gripe3_a: That's why we show the math: after every match, you see exactly what changed and why — even when the number doesn't feel right.
home_rating_p: No questionnaire, no guessed value: PadelIndex calculates from opponent strength, score margin and confirmation by the opposing team — with the exact same code that runs the live ratings. Try the rating simulator yourself.
home_tokens_p: You earn tokens for every confirmed match. Redeem them at your club — for coaching sessions, equipment, or entry fees. Like frequent-flyer miles, just for padel.
home_vereine_h2: The rating runs on your own site.
home_vereine_p_pre: From here on it's not about your own level anymore, it's about your club — if you're only here as a player right now,
home_vereine_p_post: above is already everything you need. For clubs: one line of code, and the ranking runs on your website, in your colors, with zero plugin chaos.
home_liga_h2: Real club leagues run on PadelIndex too.
home_liga_p: The BÁVARO PADEL LEAGUE at STC Oberland plays in 4-player boxes with rotating doubles partners, its own box standings and promotion/relegation — a standalone ranking alongside the general PadelIndex level. Results also feed into the Index rating.
home_ratgeber_h2: Rules, equipment, technique and tactics, explained simply.
home_ratgeber_p: The PadelIndex guides cover everything from your first serve to doubles tactics — and the quiz, with three difficulty levels, lets you test how confident you really are.
home_cta_p: Set up your player profile — with your real name, club, and a password. Your first confirmed match gives you your first level.
hseq_note: Calculated with the model that runs in production — opponent strength, score margin, and how well the system already knows you.
rating_meta_title: How the PadelIndex rating is calculated — a level from confirmed matches
rating_meta_description: No questionnaire, no self-assessment: PadelIndex calculates your padel level from opponent strength, score margin and confidence — with the exact same model that rates every match in production. Try the rating simulator.
rating_og_title: How the PadelIndex rating is calculated
rating_og_description: A level from confirmed matches instead of self-assessment: opponent strength, score margin and confidence, explained clearly.
rating_intro_p: Turn the values and hit calculate. It's computed with the exact same code that runs the live ratings — including the doubles logic: the less the system knows someone, the more their rating moves. Set a player's match count to zero and watch.
rating_factor1_p: A win against a stronger duo says more than one against a weaker one. Surprises carry the most information, so they weigh the most.
rating_factor2_p: 6:0, 6:0 is a different statement than 7:6, 5:7, 7:5. The score margin factors into every calculation — a close loss against strong opponents costs you almost nothing.
rating_factor3_p: Your rating swings a lot at first, on purpose: after roughly ten to fifteen matches your range settles. After that, it's just fine-tuning.
rating_cta1_pre: That was just the simulation — your real level needs a real match.
rating_cta2_pre: Not sure yet roughly where you stand?
rating_sicherheit_h2: The more you play, the more precise your level gets.
rating_sicherheit_p: We don't store a single number for you, but a distribution: an estimate of your ability plus the uncertainty around it. What's shown is deliberately the cautious edge — if you've played little, you'd rather be underestimated than overestimated.
rating_verlauf_p: Not a drawn graph: these fourteen matches ran one after another through the real model — from the first entry as an unknown player to the end of the provisional phase.

faq_meta_title: Frequently Asked Questions about PadelIndex — Rating, Level & Clubs
faq_meta_description: All the answers about PadelIndex: padel rating and level calculation, player profiles, club rankings, league, finding playing partners, tokens and pricing — sorted by topic.
faq_og_description: Rating, level, player profiles, club rankings, league and more — every answer in one place.
faq_intro_pre: All the answers about rating, player profiles, clubs, league and more — sorted by topic. Missing something?
faq_search_empty: No questions found. Try a different search term.
faq_ue_a1: PadelIndex is an independent rating platform for amateur padel players. Your level comes from confirmed matches — opponent strength, score margin, and how confident we already are in your level — not from a questionnaire or a self-assessment. See exactly how it works on [the rating page](/rating).
faq_ue_a2: For anyone who wants to know how strong they really play — whether a complete beginner or a tournament player. And for clubs that want a ranking on their own website without maintaining it by hand.
faq_ue_a3: Levels are usually guessed or ticked on a questionnaire — and then only valid within one club or app. PadelIndex instead calculates from real, confirmed results, across clubs and in a way you can trace back.
faq_ue_q4: What sets PadelIndex apart from a self-assessment or plain Elo?
faq_ue_a4: With PadelIndex, the other side confirms every result, the score margin counts (6:0 weighs differently than 7:6), and in doubles each player's value moves individually instead of treating the team as one unit. The [full comparison](/rating#vergleich) lays out every difference side by side.
faq_ue_a5: Yes. PadelIndex is an independent platform, not tied to any padel federation, league, or specific club.
faq_ue_a6: PadelIndex is developed by Alec Hahn, part of the family business Sportcenter Hahn GmbH, active in sports facilities and sports operations for many years. More on the [about page](/ueber).
faq_pr_q1: How do I create a player profile?
faq_pr_a1: Through [registration](/registrieren) — with first name, last name, date of birth, your club, email address and password. Once you've confirmed your email, you can sign in and use your profile.
faq_pr_q2: What information do I need to register?
faq_pr_a2: First and last name, date of birth, club name, email address, and a password of at least eight characters. Your date of birth stays private and is never shown publicly.
faq_pr_q3: How do I confirm my email address?
faq_pr_a3: After registering, you automatically get an email with a confirmation link. Your account only becomes active once you click it. If no email arrives or the link expired, you can request a new one [from the sign-in page](/login).
faq_pr_q4: How can I edit my profile?
faq_pr_a4: In [your account](/konto) you can add your city, playing hand, preferred side, gender, and an optional self-assessment (0–7), plus upload a profile picture. Your rating itself can't be edited there — it comes exclusively from confirmed matches.
faq_pr_q5: How do I claim my profile?
faq_pr_a5: If your name is already on a club ranking, you don't need to create a new profile: on the club page (e.g. [STC Oberland](/c/stc-oberland/beanspruchen)) you enter your name, confirm by email link that you're that person — and take over the existing profile along with its rating and match history.
faq_pr_q6: What happens if a profile with my name already exists?
faq_pr_a6: If several profiles in the same club share a name, your club admin reviews the match by hand before approving it — your profile status shows "awaiting review" in the meantime. If a request was rejected, for example because the name wasn't unambiguous, reach out to your club's management.
faq_pr_q7: Who can see my profile data, and can I hide my full name?
faq_pr_a7: Publicly visible are your display name, rating, matches, and any optional details you enter yourself. Date of birth and email address are always private. Once your profile is claimed, [your account](/konto) lets you choose whether your full name shows publicly or only a shortened form, e.g. "M. Kaiser".
faq_pr_q8: What are the badges on my profile?
faq_pr_a8: Your public profile can show badges calculated automatically from your matches: "10 Siege in Folge" (ten confirmed wins in a row), "Most Improved Player" (the biggest rating gain in your club over the last 30 days), and "Mixed Specialist" (five or more confirmed mixed matches) — these labels show as-is regardless of the site language. There are exactly these three today; more are planned according to the [roadmap](/roadmap).
faq_ra_a1: From every confirmed match: who you beat, how clear-cut it was, and how many matches we already know about you. A win against a stronger pair counts for more than one against a weaker pair, and the score margin factors in too — a close loss against strong opponents costs you almost nothing. The [rating simulator](/rating) calculates live with the exact same model that runs in production.
faq_ra_q2: What does the confidence of my rating mean?
faq_ra_a2: PadelIndex doesn't just store a single number but a distribution: an estimate of your level plus the uncertainty around it. What's shown is deliberately the cautious edge of that range — someone who's played little is underestimated rather than overestimated. The ring next to your rating on your profile shows this confidence as a percentage; more under [confidence](/rating#sicherheit).
faq_ra_q3: How many matches do I need for a meaningful rating?
faq_ra_a3: After roughly ten to fifteen matches your range settles down reasonably — until then your rating counts as provisional and swings more. That's intentional: it lets the system figure out where you really stand much faster.
faq_ra_q4: Can my rating drop, and what happens with mismatched doubles partners?
faq_ra_a4: Yes — losses lower your rating just as wins raise it, depending on opponent strength and score margin. In doubles, the team isn't scored as one unit; each player moves individually: whoever is rated lower or has fewer matches moves more with every result than their partner does.
faq_ra_q5: How up to date is my rating?
faq_ra_a5: It updates with every confirmed match, in real time — there's no daily or weekly recalculation, just an immediate one after each confirmed result.
faq_ra_q6: What is the level estimator, and how does it differ from the real rating?
faq_ra_a6: The [level estimator](/level-schaetzen) is a short questionnaire — six questions, no sign-up — that gives a rough placement of your playing level on the 0–7 scale. It doesn't replace a real rating, which comes exclusively from confirmed matches, but only serves as a suggestion for the optional self-assessment on your profile.
faq_ma_q1: How do I report a match?
faq_ma_a1: Via your club page under "Report match", reachable from [your account](/konto): enter your partner, both opponents, and the set scores, then submit. This requires you and all four players to belong to the same club.
faq_ma_a2: Your reported result counts as confirmed as soon as one person from the opposing team agrees to it — or automatically after 48 hours if no one responds. Only a confirmed match changes ratings.
faq_ma_q3: What happens if the other side doesn't respond?
faq_ma_a3: After 48 hours without a response, the result is automatically confirmed. This stops a match from staying "pending" forever just because someone forgot to confirm.
faq_ma_q4: What match types are there, and do federation matches count too?
faq_ma_a4: When reporting, you pick a type: casual, GPS (official points matches organized by the German Padel Federation), tournament, club league, or PadelIndex challenge. All types feed into your rating — the type is just for organizing your match history.
faq_ma_q5: Which matches count toward my rating?
faq_ma_a5: Every confirmed match between four registered players of the same club, regardless of match type. Unconfirmed or cancelled matches don't count.
faq_mi_q1: How do I find playing partners on PadelIndex?
faq_mi_a1: Under ["Find players"](/spieler-finden) you see everyone with saved playing times, sorted by overlap with your own times, rating, club, and desired match type. From there you can send a play request directly.
faq_mi_q2: What are playing times and play requests?
faq_mi_a2: Under ["My playing times"](/spielzeiten) you enter when you have time to play — others never see these times directly, they only feed into suggestions. If someone sends you a play request through this, you'll find it under ["Requests"](/anfragen) and can accept or decline it.
faq_mi_a3: Through [challenges](/challenges) you can challenge higher-ranked players at your club to a match. A win doesn't swap ranking positions — it simply affects your rating like any other match.
faq_mi_a4: Padel Roulette is a simple format for clubs: the club sets up a time slot, members sign up — once four people have signed up, the match happens. No group-chat coordination needed.
faq_ve_q1: How can my club join PadelIndex?
faq_ve_a1: We're onboarding clubs one at a time — STC Oberland is currently our pilot club. If your club wants in, you can [request a demo under "For clubs"](/vereine#demo).
faq_ve_a2: A ranking that your players fill in themselves — you don't maintain any results by hand. The ranking can be embedded on your own club website with one line of code, in your colors. Plan details are [under "For clubs"](/vereine).
faq_ve_q3: What can a club admin manage?
faq_ve_a3: In their own club area, a club admin manages members — adding, removing, approving or rejecting profile claims —, cancels incorrectly reported matches, sets up Padel Roulette time slots, maintains the token rewards catalog, and can calibrate a starting level for new members without match history.
faq_ve_q4: How are player profiles assigned to a club?
faq_ve_a4: Either a player signs up themselves through registration, or the club admin creates a placeholder profile for someone without an account — which can later be claimed through the club page. Both paths go through the same club approval once a claim is pending.
faq_ve_q5: How is the ranking embedded on a club's own website?
faq_ve_a5: With one line of embedded code, the ranking runs directly on your website — it works in WordPress, Elementor, Wix, and practically any system that allows HTML, and stays visually independent of your theme.
faq_rl_q1: How does the club ranking work?
faq_rl_a1: Every club page, for example [STC Oberland](/c/stc-oberland), shows all members sorted by rating, with each one's confidence level. It updates automatically with every confirmed match.
faq_rl_q2: What criteria sort players, and why does my position change?
faq_rl_a2: By rating alone. Your position changes whenever your rating or another player's rating changes through new confirmed matches — not simply through the passage of time or inactivity.
faq_rl_q3: What does "imported from league results" mean?
faq_rl_a3: Where a ranking isn't yet based on matches reported through PadelIndex but on results imported from an existing league table, we say so openly with a notice — instead of faking a currency it doesn't have.
faq_rl_q4: What is the PadelIndex league (box league), and how does it differ from your level?
faq_rl_a4: In [a league](/liga/bavaro), small groups called boxes play round-robin against each other; scoring is by match points, sets, and games — that's the league score, not the same as your PadelIndex level. Results additionally feed into your level. Boxes from different leagues or cycles are never compared directly.
faq_rl_q5: How do I join a league?
faq_rl_a5: Through [the league page](/liga/bavaro) or your account, you put yourself on the waitlist. A spot in a box is always assigned by hand by the club admin — signing up isn't an automatic assignment. At the end of a cycle, the system proposes promotions and relegations, which the club must confirm before they take effect.
faq_ka_q1: What does the PadelIndex map show?
faq_ka_a1: [The map](/karte) lists padel venues, highlights PadelIndex partner clubs, and also shows an operable list below the map — for screen readers and without a mouse. It doesn't claim to be complete.
faq_ka_q2: What does "partner" mean on the map?
faq_ka_a2: A partner is a club that actively uses PadelIndex — with its own ranking and player profiles. Venues without that status are listed but not yet active on PadelIndex.
faq_ka_q3: My venue is missing or listed incorrectly — what do I do?
faq_ka_a3: Write to us at kontakt@padelindex.de and we'll add or correct the entry. If you run the venue yourself and want to use PadelIndex, ["For clubs"](/vereine#demo) is the direct next step.
faq_to_q1: What are tokens, and how do I earn them?
faq_to_a1: Tokens are a balance you earn for confirmed matches, for example for playing or for wins. You see your balance and history in [your account](/konto).
faq_to_q2: What can I do with tokens?
faq_to_a2: If your club has set up a rewards catalog, you can redeem tokens there for rewards, for example a coaching session — directly in your account.
faq_to_q3: Do tokens expire, or can I transfer them?
faq_to_a3: No. Tokens are a pure balance: no transferring to other players, no expiry through losses.
faq_pi_q1: What does "pilot phase" mean at PadelIndex?
faq_pi_a1: PadelIndex is currently being tested day to day with real players and first pilot clubs, rather than launching with a long feature list. Foundation first, then the platform — more on the [roadmap](/roadmap).
faq_pi_a2: Registration and profiles, match reporting with confirmation, rating calculation, club rankings with a club admin area, profile claiming, the league with boxes, matchmaking (playing times, play requests, challenges, Padel Roulette), tokens and rewards, the map, plus the level estimator, guides, and quiz — everything described on this page already runs in production.
faq_pi_a3: According to the [roadmap](/roadmap), among others: expanded matchmaking by location and availability, more club and league management, further statistics, and eventually cross-club and regional rankings. None of this is available yet — the roadmap describes a direction, not fixed dates.
faq_pi_q4: How can I give feedback or support PadelIndex?
faq_pi_a4: The simplest way: play, report your matches, and tell us what's missing or not working. The more confirmed results come together, the more accurate the rating gets for everyone. Feedback goes to kontakt@padelindex.de.
faq_da_q1: What data does PadelIndex store about me?
faq_da_a1: Name, date of birth (private), email address, club membership, and the matches and results your rating is built from. Optional details like city, playing hand, or self-assessment are ones you enter yourself. Details are in the [privacy policy](/datenschutz).
faq_da_q2: How do I report incorrect information or a wrongly assigned profile?
faq_da_a2: Write to us at kontakt@padelindex.de — for example if a result is attributed incorrectly or a profile isn't yours.
faq_da_q3: How do I get my profile removed from the ranking?
faq_da_a3: Through ["I don't want to be listed here"](/profil-entfernen), linked directly on every profile page. It works without logging in: you enter the profile name and your email address and confirm by link — as soon as you open it, the profile disappears immediately from the public ranking.
faq_da_q4: Where do I find the full privacy policy?
faq_da_a4: At [/datenschutz](/datenschutz), with full details on the data controller, services used, and your rights.
faq_ko_a1: Yes, always — there's no cost for players.
faq_ko_q2: What does PadelIndex cost for clubs?
faq_ko_a2: There's a free tier plus two paid plans, Basic and Pro, with more features. Founding clubs play free for the first twelve months, regardless of plan. Details [under "For clubs"](/vereine).
faq_ko_q3: What's included in the free club tier?
faq_ko_a3: The club's top 10, public player profiles, and a PadelIndex mention on the ranking.
faq_ko_q4: What do Basic and Pro add?
faq_ko_a4: Basic adds the full table, filters by level, gender, and time period, your own club colors and logo, and importing league results. Pro adds level-based match finding, the token rewards catalog, a custom subdomain, and the option to turn off the PadelIndex mention.
faq_hi_q1: Where do I get help if I'm stuck?
faq_hi_a1: Write to us any time at kontakt@padelindex.de — whether it's a technical problem, a question about your profile, or something missing from this FAQ.
faq_hi_q2: How do I report a technical bug?
faq_hi_a2: Also by email at kontakt@padelindex.de, ideally with a short description of what you did and what happened instead.
faq_hi_q3: How can my club get in touch?
faq_hi_a3: Through [the demo form under "For clubs"](/vereine#demo) or directly by email at kontakt@padelindex.de.
org_description: Independent level ranking for amateur padel players, calculated from confirmed matches instead of self-assessment.
ueber_meta_description: PadelIndex is a project by Alec Hahn (Sportcenter Hahn GmbH) — a rating for amateur padel players from confirmed matches, no questionnaire and no club directory.
ueber_og_description: A rating for amateur padel players from confirmed matches — who's behind PadelIndex and why it exists.
ueber_h1: Orientation for the growing padel community.
ueber_intro_p1: PadelIndex is a platform for everyone who plays padel in Germany and wants to know how strong they really are.
ueber_intro_p2: Our goal is simple: a level built from real, confirmed matches — not from self-assessment or a number that never moves. From your own rating to your club's ranking to the question of how you'd really stack up against a specific team — PadelIndex aims to be the go-to place for your level in German padel.
ueber_praxis_h2: From the field, for the field
ueber_praxis_p1: Behind PadelIndex is Alec Hahn, developer and part of the family business Sportcenter Hahn GmbH.
ueber_praxis_p1b: Christopher Hahn, managing director of Sportcenter Hahn GmbH, contributed to testing (QA) the platform.
ueber_praxis_p2: The Hahn family has worked in operating and developing sports facilities for decades. Sportcenter Hahn connects sport, club life, and professional sports infrastructure, giving direct insight into what players and clubs actually need.
ueber_praxis_p3: To us, padel is more than just another trend sport. The dynamism, the community, and the sport's rapid growth in Germany hold enormous potential — but also raise the question of how to compare your own level across club boundaries at all. PadelIndex aims to solve exactly that: a rating that's explainable and grows with every match.
ueber_anspruch_p1: We don't want to build a complicated rating system, but one that's trusted.
ueber_claim_line1: Play. Confirm. Know where you stand.
ueber_value_nachvollziehbarkeit_t: every change to your level is explained, no black box.
ueber_value_bestaetigung_t: a result only counts once the opposing team agrees.
ueber_value_transparenz_t: the same code in the rating simulator as in production.
ueber_value_community_t: a rating lives from the players and clubs who take part.
ueber_value_wachstum_t: we grow with every club that joins.
ueber_gemeinsam_p1: Padel is growing fast in Germany. At the same time, almost no club has a reliable way to place its members' level beyond its own courts. That's exactly where PadelIndex comes in.
ueber_gemeinsam_p2: We're starting with a pilot club in the Oberland region (STC Oberland) and want to grow from there — club by club, match by match.
ueber_gemeinsam_p3_pre: If you represent a club that wants to join, spot an error in your profile, or have an idea for the platform, we'd love to hear from you at
ueber_claim_line2: Padel is growing. We make your level visible.
ds_p2: PadelIndex processes two kinds of personal data: the email address you provide when joining the waitlist or registering, and the public ranking data of padel players (name or abbreviated name, level, match results). Both are described separately below.
ds_p3: This website runs on Cloudflare Workers. Cloudflare necessarily processes technical connection data (including IP address, time of access, requested page) in order to deliver the website at all. The legal basis is our legitimate interest in stable, secure operation (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). This access data is not linked to ranking or account data.
ds_p4_intro: We use the following external services, which act as processors on our behalf:
ds_p4_supabase_desc: (database, login) — stores all account, ranking, and match data.
ds_p4_supabase_status: Server location and status of the data processing agreement: to be added.
ds_p4_cloudflare_desc: (hosting, delivery) — delivers the website and processes technical connection data for that purpose (see section 3).
ds_p4_cloudflare_status: Legal basis for the data transfer: to be added.
ds_p4_resend_desc: (transactional emails) — sends emails on our behalf that are necessary for operation (e.g. confirmation links, notifications about play requests and challenges). Resend receives the email address and content of each message for that purpose.
ds_p5_pre: If you join the waitlist on padelindex.de, we store your email address and, if provided, your club's name, in order to inform you about the start of the pilot and to reach out to your club directly. The entry only becomes active once you click the confirmation link in the email (double opt-in) — until then, the address is only provisionally noted. The legal basis is your consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR). You can withdraw this consent at any time, informally, by email to
ds_p5_post: ; we then delete the entry immediately.
ds_p6: If a club requests a demo via the form in the clubs area, we store the club name, contact person, email address, and an optional message in order to process the request. The legal basis is the initiation of a contractual relationship (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR).
ds_p7_1: At the core of PadelIndex is a publicly viewable ranking per club: name (or abbreviated for profiles not yet claimed, e.g. "Robin K."), level value, number of matches, and a rough form trend.
ds_p7_2_bold: registered players who signed up themselves
ds_p7_2_post: the processing for providing the ranking is part of contract performance (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR) — anyone who registers does so explicitly in order to appear in a ranking.
ds_p7_3_post: and have not yet been claimed by the person concerned, no consent yet exists. Here we rely on our legitimate interest in making existing league results visible and comparable (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR) — for this reason, these names are always shown abbreviated only, never in full. You can object to this at any time (Art. 21 GDPR, see section 9) — your profile then disappears from the public view, without needing an account to do so.
ds_p8: We use only technically necessary cookies to keep you logged in after signing in (Supabase Auth session cookie). There are currently no analytics, marketing, or tracking cookies and no advertising networks on this site.
ds_p9: We store account and ranking data for as long as your account or profile exists. We store waitlist entries until the pilot launches or until you withdraw. After a deletion or a successful objection (sections 6 and 9), we remove the affected data from public view immediately; complete removal from backups happens as part of the usual backup cycles.
ds_p10_intro: You have the right, at any time, to:
ds_p10_1_pre: access to the data stored about you (Art. 15 GDPR), correction of inaccurate data (Art. 16 GDPR), erasure (Art. 17 GDPR), restriction of processing (Art. 18 GDPR), data portability (Art. 20 GDPR), and objection to processing based on legitimate interest (Art. 21 GDPR). For your own public player profile, you'll find a direct "I don't want to be listed here" link on your profile page that works without logging in. For anything else, an email to
ds_p10_2: You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority. The authority responsible for us is the Bavarian State Office for Data Protection Supervision (BayLDA).
ds_p11: Transmission between your browser and our servers is TLS-encrypted throughout (https). Access to account data and non-public profile data is restricted via access rules (Row Level Security) at the database level.

rl_summary: What do level and confidence mean?
rl_level_text: is a number from 0 to 7, calculated from confirmed matches. The higher it is, the stronger the estimated playing level.
rl_confidence_text: shows how reliable the value is. With few matches it's low and the level can still jump a lot — with more confirmed results it rises.
